conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do I divide a whole number by a fraction?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. In this group we go deeper: trickier numbers, a second way to see it, and explaining why it works — not just getting the answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal (the fraction flipped over) — and you can explain why it works, even when it gets tricky.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: Agent Park has 4 pounds of powder and each bag holds 1/2 pound. I want 4 ÷ 1/2.
Keep the 4. Change ÷ to ×. Flip 1/2 to make 2/1, which is just 2.
So 4 ÷ 1/2 = 8. He can fill 8 bags. That makes sense: each pound fills 2 bags, and 4 pounds × 2 = 8.

explore.instructions: Go deeper: Use the number line to show how many 1/2-size jumps fit into 4. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

discourse.prompt: Why does 4 ÷ 1/2 = 8? How does the number line show this?

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication. Are we finding groups or finding how many pieces fit?
Division by a fraction asks 'how many fit,' not multiplication.
That's computing division by whole numbers. Remember: dividing by 1/3 is different.
hints: The divisor is 2/3 — not a unit fraction — so the flip matters even more here.
Keep 6, change ÷ to ×, and flip the whole fraction 2/3 (both numbers trade places).
2/3 flips to 3/2, giving 6 × 3/2. Multiply, then simplify the result before choosing.
onLevel.explanationEs: 6 ÷ 2/3 = 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. Mantén el 6, cambia ÷ por × e invierte 2/3 a 3/2.
hintsEs: El divisor es 2/3, que no es una fracción unitaria, así que invertir importa aún más aquí.
Conserva el 6, cambia ÷ por × e invierte la fracción completa 2/3 (los dos números cambian de lugar).
2/3 se invierte a 3/2, y queda 6 × 3/2. Multiplica y luego simplifica el resultado antes de elegir.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Keep, Change, Flip
workedExample.work: Flipped the wrong number — wrote 1/8 × 3/4 instead of 8 × 4/3

onLevel.correctWork: Keep the dividend 8 the same and flip only the divisor: 8 × 4/3 = 32/3 = 10 2/3. The mistake was flipping the whole number 8 into 1/8 instead of flipping the divisor 3/4 into 4/3.
hints: Only the divisor (the fraction you are dividing by) gets flipped — the 8 stays as 8.
onLevel.explanation: Only the divisor gets flipped. The Keep, Change, Flip step turned the dividend 8 into 1/8 and left 3/4 alone, which is backwards; the correct rewrite is 8 × 4/3 = 32/3 = 10 2/3. Since 3/4 is less than 1, more than 8 of those pieces fit into 8 wholes, so a tiny answer like 3/32 cannot be right.
onLevel.explanationEs: Solo se invierte el divisor. En el paso de Conservar, Cambiar, Invertir se convirtió el dividendo 8 en 1/8 y se dejó 3/4 igual, que es al revés; la reescritura correcta es 8 × 4/3 = 32/3 = 10 2/3. Como 3/4 es menor que 1, en 8 enteros caben más de 8 de esas piezas, así que una respuesta tan pequeña como 3/32 no puede ser correcta.

onLevel.title: Find the Division Error
onLevel.correctWork: 6 × 3/2 (flip the divisor 2/3 to get 3/2, not keep it as 2/3). Then 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9.
hints: In 'Keep, Change, Flip' — which fraction gets flipped?
The divisor (2/3) should become its reciprocal (3/2). Did Step 2 flip the right fraction?
onLevel.explanation: The Keep, Change, Flip step kept the divisor as 2/3 instead of flipping it to its reciprocal 3/2. The correct work is 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. Nine also makes sense as a count: each whole holds one and a half 2/3-size pieces, so 6 wholes hold 9 of them — more than the 6 you started with, not less.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso de Conservar, Cambiar, Invertir se dejó el divisor como 2/3 en vez de invertirlo a su recíproco 3/2. El trabajo correcto es 6 × 3/2 = 18/2 = 9. El 9 también tiene sentido como conteo: cada entero contiene una pieza y media de 2/3, así que 6 enteros contienen 9 de ellas, más que el 6 inicial, no menos.

onLevel.prompt: A pizza shop has 8 whole pizzas. Each serving is 2/3 of a pizza. How many servings can they make? Write and solve an equation, then explain why the answer is greater than 8.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The equation is 8 ÷ 2/3 = ___. Using Keep, Change, Flip: 8 × 3/2 = ___. The answer is greater than 8 because ___.
onLevel.hint: Compare dividing by 2 (whole) vs dividing by 1/2 (fraction). Why is one answer bigger?
hints: Re-read: 8 whole pizzas, and each serving takes 2/3 of one pizza — servings are smaller than a pizza.
Set up total ÷ serving size, use Keep, Change, Flip, then explain why the count beats 8.
Flip 2/3 to 3/2 and set up 8 × 3/2. Finish it, then explain: each pizza serves more than one person, so…
onLevel.explanation: The question asks how many 2/3-pizza servings fit in 8 pizzas, so the equation is 8 ÷ 2/3. Keep, change, flip gives 8 × 3/2 = 24/2 = 12 servings. The count beats 8 because each serving is smaller than a whole pizza, so every pizza makes more than one serving.
onLevel.explanationEs: La pregunta es cuántas porciones de 2/3 de pizza caben en 8 pizzas, así que la ecuación es 8 ÷ 2/3. Conservar, cambiar, invertir da 8 × 3/2 = 24/2 = 12 porciones. El resultado supera a 8 porque cada porción es menor que una pizza entera, así que cada pizza rinde más de una porción.
onLevel.promptEs: Una pizzería tiene 8 pizzas enteras. Cada porción es 2/3 de una pizza. ¿Cuántas porciones pueden hacer? Escribe y resuelve una ecuación y después explica por qué la respuesta es mayor que 8.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer: 8 pizzas enteras y cada porción usa 2/3 de una pizza; las porciones son más pequeñas que una pizza.
Plantea total ÷ tamaño de la porción, usa Conserva, Cambia, Invierte y luego explica por qué el conteo pasa de 8.
Invierte 2/3 a 3/2 y plantea 8 × 3/2. Termínalo y luego explica: cada pizza alcanza para más de una persona, así que…

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Catch the Catering Mistake
extending.correctWork: Keep the 6 and flip the divisor 3/4 to its reciprocal 4/3: 6 × 4/3 = 24/3 = 8 bowls. The mistake was multiplying by 3/4 instead of flipping it to 4/3.
hints: In Keep, Change, Flip, the second fraction (the divisor) is the one that gets flipped.
Flip 3/4 to 4/3 before multiplying — 6 × 4/3, not 6 × 3/4.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: atrapa el error del banquete
extending.explanation: The Keep, Change, Flip step changed the sign but kept 3/4 instead of flipping it to 4/3, which is why the answer came out smaller than 6 instead of larger. The correct work is 6 × 4/3 = 24/3 = 8 bowls. Since each bowl holds less than a full cup, 6 cups must fill more than 6 bowls.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso de Conservar, Cambiar, Invertir se cambió el signo pero se dejó 3/4 en vez de invertirlo a 4/3, y por eso la respuesta salió menor que 6 en lugar de mayor. El trabajo correcto es 6 × 4/3 = 24/3 = 8 tazones. Como cada tazón contiene menos de una taza completa, 6 tazas deben llenar más de 6 tazones.

Use Keep, Change, Flip: keep the 6, change ÷ to ×, and flip the divisor 1/3.

hintsEs: 6 ÷ 1/3 pregunta cuántas piezas de tamaño 1/3 caben en 6 enteros. Predice: ¿mayor o menor que 6?
Usa Conserva, Cambia, Invierte: conserva el 6, cambia ÷ por × e invierte el divisor 1/3.
Al invertir, 1/3 se vuelve 3/1. Plantea 6 × 3 y termina la multiplicación.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Divide Whole Numbers by Fractions is doing 'Keep, Change' but skipping the 'Flip' — students multiply by the divisor as it is instead of by its reciprocal. For example, for 6 ÷ 3/4, a student might write 6 × 3/4 = 4 1/2 and stop there, but the divisor 3/4 must be flipped to 4/3 first: 6 × 4/3 = 24/3 = 8. Before you submit, check: did I flip the second fraction (the divisor) upside down before multiplying?

diagram.title: Marker Sections in One Foot
diagram.caption: One foot of rope splits into four 1/4-foot markers, so each whole foot makes 4 markers and all 10 feet make 10 x 4 = 40 (10 divided by 1/4 = 40).

connect.scenario: A detective has 10 feet of rope to section off a crime scene. Each section needs to be 1/4 of a foot long for detailed evidence markers. How many markers can the detective set up?
connect.promptQuestion: How does dividing a whole number by a fraction help the detective?
connect.prompt: The detective can set up ___ markers because 10 ÷ 1/4 = ___.

check.explanation: Each foot of rope makes 4 quarter-foot markers, so 10 × 4 = 40. In symbols: 10 ÷ 1/4 = 10 × 4/1 = 40.
The reciprocal flips the fraction: 1/4 becomes 4/1 = 4. Dividing by 1/4 is the same as multiplying by 4.

check.stem: A student answered 2.5. What did they do wrong?
choices: They divided by 4 instead of by 1/4
They used the wrong rope length
check.explanation: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5, but the markers are 1/4 foot each, not 4 feet each. Dividing by 1/4 means multiplying by 4, which gives 40.

connect.modelAnswer: 10 ÷ 1/4 = 40 markers. Each foot of rope makes 4 quarter-foot markers, so 10 × 4 = 40. Dividing by 1/4 is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal, 4.

choiceFeedback: That's multiplication. Are we finding groups or finding how many pieces fit?

hints: 9 ÷ 1/3 asks how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 9 wholes — predict more or fewer than 9 first.
Keep, Change, Flip: keep the 9, change ÷ to ×, and flip 1/3 before multiplying.

questions.stem: Which expression means 'how many 1/3-size pieces are in 2'?
questions.explanation: Finding how many 1/3-size pieces fit into 2 is represented by 2 ÷ 1/3. The answer is 6.
6 ÷ 1/5 means how many 1/5-size pieces fit into 6. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 6 × 5 = 30.

questions.stem: A rope is 4 feet long. How many 1/2-foot pieces can be cut from it?
questions.explanation: 4 ÷ 1/2 = 4 × 2 = 8 pieces. Each whole foot contains 2 halves, and 4 × 2 = 8.
3 ÷ 1/4 asks: how many 1/4-size pieces fit into 3? The answer is 12, because each whole has 4 fourths, and 3 × 4 = 12.
